item.title: CedarLogic 0.4 (build 1702) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic 0.4 for Mac, beta 2 (build 1702). Get it from inside CedarLogic: Help > Check for Updates.

New in beta 2

A new intro. The first time you open CedarLogic, and the first time after an update, a short intro plays: the circuit draws itself, the light comes on, and a chime plays. Click or press a key to skip it. Help > Play the Intro plays it again any time. If you like it, Settings > General has "Play the intro every time CedarLogic opens". It plays without the chime then.

Actions on the right. A strip down the right edge of the window holds the things you use most, one click away. In Settings > Actions you can show it on screen, put the same buttons in the toolbar, or hide it. Search there to find an action, and right-click the strip to choose your own. Drag one up or down to change the order. Fold it away and it opens when the mouse reaches the right edge. In Focus mode it folds to a small tab. View > Show Actions (Control-Command-S) opens and folds it. If you used CedarLogic before, it starts hidden: turn it on with View > Show Actions.

The menus work right away. File > Export as Image and the other menu items are ready as soon as the app opens. You no longer need to click the circuit first.

Welcome and What's New stay closed. They no longer open again over your circuit the next time you start the app.

What's new

On every computer

Recently Deleted. Deleting a circuit from Your Circuits no longer ends it. Open "Recently Deleted" in Your Circuits to see what you deleted, newest first. Restore puts a circuit back. Delete Now removes it for good, and asks first. Circuits stay for 30 days, then they go. They stay on that computer. They aren't synced. (Mac, Windows, Linux.)

Clear Drawing asks first. Clearing all the drawing on a page now asks "Clear all drawing on this page?" and tells you Undo brings it back. (Mac, Windows, Linux.)

Send Feedback has a daily limit. You can send 10 reports a day. A short summary is needed before Send turns on. If you reach the limit, you can ask for more with "Request more" and say why in a line. You can ask once a day, and it gives you 10 more. (Mac, Windows, Linux.)

Wires and clicks behave the same every time. Clicking where two pins sit close together, or dragging a wire at a corner, now picks the same one each time you open the app.

Connect Nearby is quicker on big pages. Holding C while you move parts, and Connect Nearby Pins, no longer stop to think for minutes on a page with thousands of parts.

Circuits save the numbers you see. Part positions are saved to a ten-thousandth of a grid square. Save, reopen and save again gives the same file.

Mac

Open the Practice Circuit. It's in the File menu and the Help menu. It opens as a new circuit of your own, called Practice Circuit.

Your sync code and class keys are in the Keychain. They used to sit in a file that backups carried along.

Crash reports say less. A report says where the app crashed. It no longer carries a trail of clicks, web addresses, or your user name in a file path.

Fixed

All apps (the shared engine)

The engine got a long round of checking: damaged files, damaged pastes and very long editing sessions. It found 40 problems and all are fixed. The ones you could have met:

  • The app no longer quits when you paste a label that has two lines.
  • A damaged .cdl file or a damaged paste no longer crashes the app, freezes it, or leaves a part connected to the wrong thing.
  • A .cdl file can no longer make a memory part read or overwrite a file on your computer when it opens.
  • A wire no longer falls into two pieces after you drag a part. Zero-length bits of wire after a drag are gone too.
  • A wire is no longer left stretched or broken after a paste.
  • Disconnecting a RAM's data pin no longer leaves a wire running to nothing.
  • Redo of Straighten Wires, Tidy Up or Build gives the same wires as the step itself.
  • A counter at its largest number, an encoder with no inputs, a wide register, and an adder, register or equivalence gate with 0 or 1 inputs no longer crash the app or read past their data.
  • A RAM no longer grows without limit when you only read it.
  • Saving the same circuit twice gives the same file.
  • A bus width or decoder size of millions in a file no longer freezes the app and runs it out of memory.
  • Cancelling Check My Circuit part way through no longer touches a circuit that has already closed.

Mac

  • Once a circuit had 500 undo steps, later changes weren't saved. They are now.
  • A change made in a gate's Settings sheet, such as a label's text, is saved. Undo and Redo save too.
  • Undo and Redo of a move, a Delete or a Disconnect give the wires back the bends you drew, not new ones.
  • Escape on a pasted copy or a new part that's still on the pointer no longer brings it back on Redo.
  • A copy put on the pointer while you're drawing can be placed.
  • Cmd-W with a sheet open no longer closes the tab or the window behind it.
  • Option-Left in the oscilloscope no longer quits the app after a long recording has been trimmed.
  • A closed circuit window now lets go of its circuit.
  • Redo of a closed tab closes the same tab after you reorder tabs.
  • Opening a damaged file whose wire lost its id shows a notice instead of crashing.
  • The first-launch sound no longer holds up the launch.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.19 (build 965) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.19 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.19-Mac.dmg below, or update from inside the app (Help › Check for Updates). macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open a downloaded copy, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new

More fixes for bugs that show up in a long session:

  • Undo takes back one thing at a time, however long you've worked. After about a quarter of an hour of editing (once the 500-step history is full), one ⌘Z could take back two changes, and pressing Escape on a paste could also remove the part placed just before it.
  • Escape means no. A paste, ⌘D copy or new part you put away with Escape no longer comes back when you press Redo.
  • Drawing and pasting. Putting a copy or a new part on the pointer while drawing now switches back to editing, so it can be placed, instead of getting stuck.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.18 (build 953) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.18 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.18-Mac.dmg below, or update from inside the app (Help › Check for Updates). macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open a downloaded copy, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new

A stability release: a week of automated testing found and fixed the bugs that showed up over a long session.

  • Closed windows stop running. A closed circuit window kept simulating in the background until you quit, so the app got slower the more circuits you opened.
  • No more crash from a damaged file. A file with one damaged wire opens with a note instead of crashing, even when it is the circuit the app reopens at launch.
  • Wires stay put. Fixed wires left off their pins after Escape mid-drag, a pin that could end up on two wires (and crash after a delete), Undo and Redo giving wires a different shape, wires on rotated parts splitting in two, pasted wires coming apart, and Tidy Up turning a RAM's wire into two dots.
  • Your work is saved. A setting changed in a part's Settings sheet is now saved and can be undone, and Undo and Redo now autosave like any other edit.
  • Smoother. The oscilloscope no longer redraws the whole window while it records, and split view's two sides stay in step when you run or pause.
  • Smaller fixes. Option-Left in the oscilloscope no longer quits; a held Space no longer gets stuck so every click pans; closing tabs closes the one you meant; Cmd-W under an open sheet beeps instead of closing a tab; the printed Classroom recovery sheet and class pass now show their content.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.17 (build 897) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.17 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.17-Mac.dmg below, or update from inside the app (Help › Check for Updates). macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open a downloaded copy, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new

  • More examples, with the inside shown. File › New from Template has new two-page examples: page 1 uses the part, page 2 builds it from gates (D, J-K and T flip-flops, 4-bit register, 3-bit counter, 4-bit adder, 2-to-4 decoder, 4-to-1 mux), plus a comparator, parity generator, edge detector and SR latch with enable.
  • Click the clock to step it. With "Only on Step Clock" on, clicking the clock part steps it. Settings › Toolbar › Step Clock shows or hides its toolbar button.
  • Export Image follows your theme. "Match Window" uses your current colours, grid and accent.
  • Sync: remove old devices from Settings › Sync › Devices, and your name now syncs across devices.
  • Classroom: share or post circuits from your own library (⌘O), and schedule class examples to release at a date and time.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.16 (build 887) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.16 (beta)

Update from inside the app (Help › Check for Updates). This beta has no disk image download.

What's new

  • Page links. Choose which pages' TO/FROM links connect: Connect All / Disconnect All Pages in the File menu, right-click a page tab › Connect to… to group pages, and coloured dots on tabs that share links. Settings › Canvas › New pages sets the default.
  • Straighten and Tidy Up fixes. They no longer drop a connection on save, never leave a wire short of its pin, draw a split as one connected wire with a dot, and cross wires a little less. Big pages straighten about twice as fast.
  • Export Image, refreshed. Preview first, with Copy Image, Save and Share. "Match Window" exports exactly what you see, dark mode included. Copied pictures now paste at the right size.
  • Class pass. Students can make a printable pass that brings them back to the class on any device; teachers can see and cancel passes.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.15 (build 876) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.15 (beta)

Update from inside the app (Help › Check for Updates). This beta has no disk image download.

What's new: Classroom, reworked (File › Classroom)

  • Share a circuit with your class. Students get "Your teacher shared …" and open it as their own copy to play with. Share an update and they can open the new version without losing theirs.
  • Class examples. Add circuits to your class's examples, sorted by topic, and release each one when you're ready. Students can open released ones anytime.
  • Simpler hand-in. An assignment opens with Instructions, Check and Hand In. Every attempt is kept for the teacher.
  • Check against your solution. Use a solution circuit as the answer key: it compares what the circuits do, not where the parts are.
  • Your classes on all your devices when Sync is on.
  • The prediction poll is gone. Show on Projector closes with Escape. The recovery sheet prints properly.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.14 (build 874) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.14 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.14-Mac.dmg below: open it and drag CedarLogic into Applications. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open it, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new: Classroom (File › Classroom)

  • Teachers: create a class and share its join code or QR code (Show on Projector puts it on the big screen). Post the circuit you have open as an assignment, with an optional answer key, and choose whether students can check their own work. See who handed in what, with each one's check result, and download them all.
  • Live class: Go Live puts your circuit on every student's screen. Ask a prediction ("what will the lights show?"), watch the answers come in, then Reveal.
  • Students: join with the code and your name, open an assignment as your own copy, check it if your teacher allows, and hand it in. When your teacher is live, a banner lets you follow along. Students can also join from the website, on an iPad, Chromebook or phone.
  • No accounts: everything is encrypted so only the teacher can read names and hand-ins.
  • From 0.3.13: presenter mode shows your pointer and selection, pulse-button clocks, drawing width control.
